# Gothic Classics

Initial source gathering: 2026-11-05. These are candidates for future creative tasks, not campaign canon or plot templates. Full Project Gutenberg texts are available at the links. Project Gutenberg identifies each as public domain in the United States; check local law before reuse elsewhere. No source text is reproduced here.

## *Carmilla* - Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu

- **Source:** [Project Gutenberg, ebook 10007](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10007); full text consulted at the linked Project Gutenberg edition on 2026-11-05.
- **Potential use:** Intimate vampire horror; the threat is experienced through hospitality, affection, illness, memory and conflicting explanations before its identity is established. Domestic routines and local rumor can make the uncanny feel close rather than distant.
- **Caution:** Its period gender and sexuality conventions are part of its historical context, not a template to reproduce. Avoid importing its character relationships, clues, or resolution as a package.

## *Dracula* - Bram Stoker

- **Source:** [Project Gutenberg, ebook 345](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/345); catalog record and synopsis consulted on 2026-11-05; full text is available but was not read for this gathering.
- **Potential use:** The epistolary form distributes knowledge across documents, voices and locations, allowing an investigation to assemble a picture no single witness possesses.
- **Caution:** Its depiction of Eastern Europe and its people reflects its period. Do not treat the novel as a reliable cultural or historical source for Barovia or Romania.

## *The Fall of the House of Usher* - Edgar Allan Poe

- **Source:** [Project Gutenberg, ebook 932](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/932); catalog record and synopsis consulted on 2026-11-05; full text is available but was not read for this gathering.
- **Potential use:** A setting's physical condition can echo and intensify a character's emotional state; uncertainty grows from the narrator's limited perspective and the house's enclosing atmosphere.
- **Caution:** Use the general technique, not its distinctive family, architecture, sequence of events or imagery.

## *Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus* - Mary Shelley

- **Source:** [Project Gutenberg, ebook 84](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/84); catalog record and synopsis consulted on 2026-11-05; full text is available but was not read for this gathering.
- **Potential use:** A feared being's perspective can complicate the audience's judgment, while creator or community responsibility creates tragedy beyond the creature's actions alone.
- **Caution:** The creature is not a vampire or werewolf analogue by default. Adapt the question of responsibility only when it fits the campaign's established metaphysics and character agency.
